Configuration File Reference ​

config.yml is the Metal configuration file, a YAML file used to configure sources, schemas, and plans.

Example config.yml

yaml
version: "0.5"

server:
  port: 3000

sources:
  my-source:
    provider: postgres
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 5432
    user: myuser
    password: myStr@ngpa$$w0rd
    database: mydatabase

schemas:
  my-schema:
    source: my-source

version v0.1+ ​

Defines the version used for the configuration. Accepted values : 0.5

Example:

yaml
version: "0.5"

server v0.1+ ​

Defines the configuration of the Metal server.

The parameters that can be configured inside the server section include:

ParameterTypeRequiredDecriptionMetal version
authenticationObjectYConfigure user authenticationv0.3+
portIntegerNServer TCP port (default: 3000)v0.1+
timezoneStringNTimezone setting (default: UTC)v0.1+
verbosityStringNLogging level (default: warn)v0.1+
cacheObjectNCache configuration(see: sources)v0.1+
request-limitStringNDefine request limit (default: 10mb)v0.1+
response-limitStringNDefine response limit (default: 10mb)v0.3+
response-rateObjectNDefine response rate limitv0.3+

Example:

yaml
server:
  port: 3000
  verbosity: debug
  cache:
    provider: mongodb
    uri: mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/
    database: metal_cache
    options:
      connectTimeoutMS: 5000
      serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000

port v0.1+ ​

Defines the Metal server's TCP port for API exposure.

Default: 3000

verbosity v0.1+ ​

Sets the console logging verbosity, which can be one of the following values:

  • trace
  • debug
  • info
  • warn
  • error

Default: warn

⚠️ IMPORTANT

Using debug or trace can significantly reduce the performance of Metal server.

cache v0.1+ ​

Sets the Database server for storing cache objects. The configuration is the same as a source. (See: sources)

This parameter must be configured if you plan to use the cache feature in Metal server.

timezone v0.1+ ​

Sets the server's timezone.

A list of acceptable timezone values can be found here.

Default: UTC

authentication v0.3+ ​

Sets the authentication configuration for the Metal server.

The parameters that can be configured inside the server section include:

ParameterTypeRequiredDecriptionMetal version
providerEnum(String)YAuthentication Provider, defaults to local (see: Authentication providers)v0.3+
default-roleStringNDefault role assigned to the user when is authenticated, defaults empty. (see: roles)v0.3+
autocreateStringNPopulate automatically users with the authenticated user if not exist, defaults to falsev0.3+

Authentication providers :

ProviderDescriptionMetal version
localEnables local authentication through Metal server using declared usersv0.3+
oidcEnables OpenID Connect authentication with an external providerv0.4+

Example:

yaml
server:
  authentication:
    type: local

ℹ️ TIP

For more informations about authentication, roles and users, please refer to the Authentication guide.

request-limit v0.1+ ​

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the bytes library for parsing. For supported values, see here.

When exeeded, an error PAYLOAD TOO LARGE(413) will occur.

Default: 10mb

response-limit v0.3+ ​

Controls the maximum response body size. If this is a number, then the value specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the bytes library for parsing. For supported values, see here.

When exeeded, an error CONTENT TOO LARGE(413) will occur.

Default: 10mb

response-rate v0.3+ ​

Controls the maximum request per window. The parameters that can be configured inside the response-rate section include:

ParameterTypeRequiredDescriptionMetal version
windowMsIntegerYThe time window for rate limiting, in milliseconds. For example, 60000 milliseconds (60 seconds).v0.3+
maxIntegerYThe maximum number of requests allowed within the windowMs time window. For example, 600 requests.v0.3+
messageStringNThe message to be sent when the rate limit is exceeded. This can be a custom message indicating that the user has made too many requests. For example, "Too many requests from this IP, please try again later."v0.3+

If exeeded, an error TOO MANY REQUEST(429) will occur.

Default:

  • windowMs: 60000
  • max: 600
  • message: Too many requests from this IP, please try again later

ai-engines v0.5+ ​

To enable AI capabilities in your Metal server, configure the following in your server configuration file:

Example

yaml
server:
  # ... other server configurations ...
  ai-engines:
    timeout: 600000
    engines-url: http://127.0.0.1:5000
    params:
      host: "127.0.0.1" # or your machine IP
      port: 2375 # exposed from docker-compose

The parameters that can be configured inside the ai-engines section include:

ParameterTypeDefault ValueRequiredDescriptionMetal Version
paramsObjectNParameters for Container Provider. By default, local Docker daemon will be used.v0.5+
build-batch-sizeInteger5NAI Engine Build batch size value.v0.5+
engines-urlURLhttp://127.0.0.1:5000YURL for AI Engine services.v0.5+
timeoutInteger60000NTimeout for AI Engine requests in milliseconds.v0.5+
min-instanceInteger1NMinimum number of AI Engine instances.v0.5+
max-instanceInteger5NMaximum number of AI Engine instances.v0.5+
cpu-scale-upInteger70NPercentage of CPU used to trigger a scale up.v0.5+
cpu-scale-downInteger30NPercentage of CPU used to trigger a scale down.v0.5+
scale-intervalInteger15000NAI Engine Scale interval value in milliseconds.v0.5+
scale-down-grace-periodInteger300000NGrace period before scaling down in milliseconds.v0.5+
cpuInteger4NCPU limit per AI Engine instances.v0.5+
memoryInteger2NMemory limit per AI Engine instances.v0.5+
cors.allowed-originsstring*NCORS allowed origins for AI Engine services.v0.5+
cors.allowed-methodsstringGET,POST,OPTIONSNCORS Allowed methods for AI Engine services.v0.5+
cors.allowed-headersstringContent-Type,Authorization,X-Requested-WithNCORS Allowed headers for AI Engine services.v0.5+

ℹ️ NOTE

For more detailed information about how to configure a Container Provider in params, See: Container Provider Configurations

roles v0.3+ ​

Sets the list of roles with associated permissions used when authentication is enabled with server.authentication. Each role is defined by a unique name and a string of permissions where each character represents a specific permission:

PermissionDescriptionMetal version
cCreate datav0.3+
rRead datav0.3+
uUpdate datav0.3+
dDelete datav0.3+
aAdministrate serverv0.3+
lList schema entitiesv0.3+

Example:

yaml
roles:
  admin: arl
  all-rights: crudla
  guest: r

users v0.1+ ​

Declares a list of Metal users used when authentication is enabled with server.authentication.

Example:

yaml
users:
  admin: 123456
  guest: "654321"

sources v0.1+ ​

This section contains all source declarations and configurations that are applied to each database server endpoint connection, much like a connection string used in development.

Every source is declared with a name, followed by the appropriate data provider configuration and options if needed.

ℹ️ NOTE

When declaring a source, the parameters that can be configured inside are: provider, host, port, user, password, database, and options.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    provider: postgres
    host: 192.168.1.113
    port: 5433
    user: root
    password: Azerty123!
    database: sampledb

  my-ms-sql-db:
    provider: mssql
    host: 192.168.1.123
    port: 1433
    user: sa
    password: Azerty123!
    database: SampleDB

The parameters that can be configured inside a source include:

ParameterTypeRequiredDecriptionMetal version
providerEnum(String)YProvider typev0.1+
databaseStringNProvider databasev0.5+
hostStringNHost serverv0.1+
portIntegerNHost portv0.1+
userStringNProvider userv0.1+
passwordStringNProvider user passwordv0.1+
optionsObjectNAdditional optionsv0.1+

provider v0.1+ ​

Defines the data provider type.

The table below describes the different values that can be configured in the provider parameter:

ValueDBMS ProviderMetal version
postgresPostgreSQLv0.1+
mssqlAzure Sql Database, Microsoft SQL Serverv0.1+
mongodbMongoDBv0.1+
planConnect to Metal Planv0.2+
storageStorage abstraction data providerv0.5+
metalMetal Server via RESTv0.2+
memoryLocal Memory storage (Non-persistant)v0.2+

For more detailed information about how to configure a data provider, See: Data Providers Configurations

ℹ️ NOTE

When using plan as a data provider, you only need to provide the name of the plan as database parameter. Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-source-from-plan:
    provider: plan
    database: my-plan

Example:

If we want to declare a source named my-postgresql-db using the PostgreSQL data provider, we write:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    provider: postgres

host v0.1+ ​

Defines the DBMS server host.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    host: 10.11.12.13

⚠️ IMPORTANT

For MongoDB, the host must be provided in the URI form mongodb://my-server:my-server-port/. Example: mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/.

ℹ️ NOTE

MS SQL Server can be provided in the form MY-SERVER\MY-INSTANCE.

port v0.1+ ​

Defines the DBMS TCP port.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    port: 5432

⚠️ IMPORTANT

This parameter is unnecessary for MongoDB.

user v0.1+ ​

Defines the user to connect to the DBMS server.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    user: root

password v0.1+ ​

Defines the DBMS user password.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    password: MySecretPassword

database v0.1+ ​

Defines the name of the database to connect to.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  my-postgresql-db:
    database: mydatabase

options v0.1+ ​

This parameter defines optional parameters to be passed to the data provider.

Example:

yaml
sources:
  mongo-db1:
    provider: mongodb
    host: mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/
    database: myDatabase
    options:
      connectTimeoutMS: 5000
      serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000

ℹ️ NOTE

For more information about how to configure a data provider and its options, See: Data Providers Configurations

schemas v0.1+ ​

This section is used to declare virtual schemas.

A schema is a mapping of DBMS source and tables mapping, and it serves as the main access point. If you want to allow access to a database or a combination of databases, you must declare your schemas here to expose them to the API.

ℹ️ NOTE

When declaring a schema, the parameters that can be configured inside are: source and entities.

⚠️ IMPORTANT

If there's no schemas declaration in config.yml, Metal server will not expose any data to the API, implying its use as a scheduled ETL tool (see: Use Case, CRON ETL).

Example:

yaml
schemas:
  my-schema1:
    source: my-mssql-db

  my-schema2:
    entities:
      my-entity1:
        source: my-mongodb-source
        entity: entity1
      my-entity2:
        source: my-postgres-source
        entity: entity2

The parameters that can be configured inside a source include:

ParameterDecriptionMetal version
sourceSource to usev0.1+
entitiesDetailed entities configurationv0.1+
anonymizeto anonymize data of given fieldsv0.3+

source v0.1+ ​

Declare which source to use from the sources section. (See: sources)

Example:

yaml
schemas:
  my-schema1:
    source: my-mssql-db

entities v0.1+ ​

Used to declare each entity from sources. It is possible to declare entities from different sources. Only declared entities are visible.

When declaring an entity, two parameters must be configured inside:

  • source: the name of a declared source
  • entity: the name of an entity that is in the source

Example:

yaml
schemas:
  my-schema2:
    entities:
      my-entity1:
        source: my-mongodb-source
        entity: entity1
      my-entity2:
        source: my-plan
        entity: entity2

ℹ️ TIP

It is possible to combine source and entities in the same schema declaration.

Example:

yaml
schemas:
  my-merged-schema:
    source: my-mssql-source
    entities:
      my-entity1:
        source: my-mongodb-source
        entity: entity1
      my-entity2:
        source: my-postgres-source
        entity: entity2

anonymize v0.3+ ​

To anonymize data of given fields. It can be unique field or a list of fields seperated with comma.

Use * value to anonymize all fields.

Please note that when using this feature all corresponding fields name of any entity from the source are anonymized.

Example

yaml
schemas:
  my-schema1:
    source: my-mssql-db
    anonymize: contact_name, company_name

⚠️ Warning

When using anonymize in a schema and in a plan, data will be anonymized twice.

~~ [Removed] ai-engines~~ v0.5+ ​

⚠️ Warning

Starting from v0.5, this configuration has been removed and managed automatically by Metal server.

plans v0.1+ ​

This section is used to declare plans which are an ETL steps. It can be used on the fly by calling a schema conneted to a plan or by scheduling as a job.

In each plan you must declare at least one entity in which the steps will be executed

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-first-entity:
    my-second-entity:

ℹ️ TIP

You may call a declared entity in the plan, in that case the steps hocked to the second entity will be executed

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-first-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: users
          fields: login, partner_id
    my-second-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: contacts
          fields: id, name, display_name
      - join:
          type: left
          entity: my-first-entity
          left-field: partner_id
          right-field: id

The steps that can be configured inside a plan can be:

Step commandDecriptionMetal version
selectto select data from an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be usedv0.1+
insertto insert data to an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be usedv0.1+
deleteto delete data from an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be usedv0.1+
updateto update data of an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be usedv0.1+
debugto enable steps debugv0.1+
breakto stop plan execution at this stepv0.1+
jointo perform data joins (Left,Right,Inner,Full outer and Cross)v0.1+
sortto sort actual datav0.1+
runto run an AI Enginev0.1+
syncto synchronize data from data source to a data destinationv0.2+
anonymizeto anonymize data of given fieldsv0.3+
list-entitiesto list entities in a schemav0.3+
remove-duplicatesto remove duplicated rowsv0.3+
pickfields to keep from actual datav0.5+
omitto remove fields from actual datav0.5+
mapto transform data using custom JavaScript codev0.5+

list-entities v0.3+ ​

To list entities in a schema. If schema is not provided, a list of actual plan's entities will be returned.

The parameters that can be configured inside select tag are :

NameDecriptionMetal version
schemaname of schemav0.3+

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - list-entities:
        schema: my-schema

📜select v0.1+ ​

To select data from an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be returned.

The parameters that can be configured inside select tag are :

NameDecriptionJS ContextMetal version
schemaname of schemaN/Av0.1+
entityname of entity in the schemaN/Av0.1+
📜fieldsfields to keep, comma seperated. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜filtercondition key:value to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜filter-expressionfree form condition to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜sortsort data, can be asc or desc. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
cachetime in seconds to cache data. (see: Optional Parameters)N/Av0.1+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - select:
        schema: demo
        entity: users
        fields: login, partner_id

📜insert v0.1+ ​

To insert data to an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be modified

The parameters that can be configured inside insert tag are :

NameDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
schemaname of schemaN/Av0.1+
entityname of entity in the schemaN/Av0.1+
📜datadata to be inserted in the entity. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - insert:
          schema: my-schema
          entity: search-engine
          data:
            - name: Google
              url: https://www.google.com
            - name: Yahoo
              url: https://www.yahoo.com
            - name: Bing
              url: https://www.bing.com

📜delete v0.1+ ​

To delete data from an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be modified

The parameters that can be configured inside delete tag are :

NameDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
schemaname of schemaN/Av0.1+
entityname of entity in the schemaN/Av0.1+
📜filtercondition key:value to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜filter-expressionfree form condition to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - delete:
          schema: my-schema
          entity: users
          filter-expression: "id >= 100"

📜update v0.1+ ​

To update data of an entity. If schema is not provided, actual plan's entity data will be modified

The parameters that can be configured inside update tag are :

NameDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
schemaname of schemaN/Av0.1+
entityname of entity in the schemaN/Av0.1+
📜filtercondition key:value to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜filter-expressionfree form condition to filter data. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜❇️datadata to be inserted in the entity. (see: Optional Parameters)$schema, $entityv0.4+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

❇️: Supports Field Escape Engine (see: Field Escape Engine)

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - update:
          schema: my-schema
          entity: users
          filter:
            is_anonymized: true
          data:
            name: "******"

debug v0.1+ ​

Enable plan steps debugging to be visible in the metadata of the JSON return. It can be one of the following values : nothing, error

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - debug:

break v0.1+ ​

To stop execution of the plan at this step.

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - break:

📜join v0.1+ ​

To perform data joins (Left,Right,Inner,Full outer and Cross)

The parameters that can be configured inside join tag are :

NameDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
📜schemaname of schema. If not provided actual plan will be used as a schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜entityname of entity in the schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
typeJoin type can be left,right,inner,full-outer,crossN/Av0.1+
📜left-fieldLeft field for equality with right-field$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜right-fieldRight field$schema, $entityv0.4+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

The type parameter can be :

ValueDescriptionMetal version
leftLeft Joinv0.1+
rightRight Joinv0.1+
innerInner Joinv0.1+
full-outerFull Outer Joinv0.1+
crossCross Joinv0.1+

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-first-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: users
          fields: login, partner_id
    my-second-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: contacts
          fields: id, name, display_name
      - join:
          type: left
          entity: my-first-entity
          left-field: partner_id
          right-field: id

sort v0.1+ ​

To sort actual plan's entity data

This command accept a list of one or many entity's fields and sorting order :

  • asc for ascending
  • desc for descending

If sorting order is not provided, ascending order will be used

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-second-entity:
      - select:
          schema: my-schema
          entity: contacts
          fields: id, name, display_name
      - sort:
          id: asc
          name: desc

[Removed] fields v0.5+ ​

⚠️ Warning

Starting from v0.5, this configuration has been renamed to pick.

pick v0.5+ ​

To keep fields from actual plan's entity data

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-first-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: users
    my-second-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: contacts
      - join:
          type: left
          entity: my-first-entity
          left-field: partner_id
          right-field: id
      - pick:
          - id
          - name
          - display_name

omit v0.5+ ​

To remove fields from actual plan's entity data

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-first-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: users
    my-second-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: contacts
      - join:
          type: left
          entity: my-first-entity
          left-field: partner_id
          right-field: id
      - omit:
          - name
          - display_name

📜map v0.5+ ​

To transform data using custom JavaScript code. The script is executed for each row in the current data table, where $row represents the current row object.

The parameters that can be configured inside map tag are :

NameTypeDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
📜scriptstringJavaScript code to transform each row$rowv0.5+
on-errorenumError handling strategy when script fails-v0.5+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

on-error options:

  • throw (default): Stop execution and throw error
  • skip: Skip the problematic row and continue processing
  • mark: Keep the row but add __map_error__ field with error message

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - select:
          schema: demo
          entity: products
      - map:
          script: |
            $row.total = $row.price * $row.quantity;
            $row.category = $row.category.toUpperCase();
            return $row;
          on-error: skip

In this example:

  • Each row gets a new total field calculated as price * quantity
  • The category field is converted to uppercase
  • The modified row is returned
  • If any row processing fails, that row is skipped and processing continues

ℹ️ INFO

The script automatically includes a return $row; statement at the end if no explicit return statement is provided. This ensures that the modified row is returned and used further in the plan execution.

⚠️ IMPORTANT

  • The script must return a valid object. If no valid object is returned, the original row will be used.
  • The script is executed in a secure sandbox environment.
  • Use on-error parameter to control error handling behavior:
    • throw (default): Stops entire map operation on first error
    • skip: Continues processing other rows, skipping problematic ones
    • mark: Keeps problematic rows with __map_error__ field containing error details

run v0.5+ ​

To run an AI Engine on actual plan's entity data.

The parameters that can be configured inside run tag are :

NameTypeDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
aistringAI Engine name (see: AI Engines)v0.1+
taskstringAI Engine task (see: AI Engines)v0.5+
paramsobjectAI Engine parameters (see: AI Engines)v0.5+
📜inputstringinput field to perform the processing$rowv0.1+
📜outputobject / stringOutput result to be stored. (see: output)$resultv0.5+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

output

It can be:

  • string representing the name of the field where the result will be stored
  • a list of key:value where key is the mapped name of the field and value is the name of result property. In this configuration JavaScript Expression Engine is supported.

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - insert:
          data:
            - url: https://tesseract.projectnaptha.com/img/eng_bw.png
            - url: https://jeroen.github.io/images/testocr.png
            - url: https://www.srcmake.com/uploads/5/3/9/0/5390645/ocr_orig.png
      - run:
          ai: ocr
          task: image-to-string
          params:
            lang: en_XX
          input: content
          output:
            ocr_text: { { $result.ocr.text } } # stores the $result.ocr.text in the `ocr_text` field
            ocr_lang_code: ${{ $result.ocr.lang.split('_')[0] }} # using JavaScript Expression Engine to transform result

📜sync v0.2+ ​

To synchronize data from source to destination. This will performs Update, Insert and Delete operations on the destination entity to be the exact copy of the data source.

The parameters that can be configured inside sync tag are :

NameDescriptionJS ContextMetal version
📜from.schemaname of source schema. If not provided actual plan will be used as a schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜from.entityname of source entity in the from.schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜to.schemaname of destination schema. If not provided actual plan will be used as a schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜to.entityname of destination entity in the to.schema$schema, $entityv0.4+
📜idfield that exists in both source and destination entity. It will be used as unique identity for synchronization$schema, $entityv0.4+

📜: Supports JavaScript Expression Engine (see: JavaScript Expression Engine)

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - sync:
          from:
            schema: srcschema
            entity: users
          to:
            schema: destschema
            entity: users
          id: user_id

anonymize v0.5+ ​

To anonymize data of given list of fields.

Example

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - anonymize:
          - contact_name
          - company_name

remove-duplicates v0.3+ ​

The remove-duplicates function is designed to remove duplicate rows from a dataset based on specified parameters. Here are the details:

ParametersTypeRequiredDescriptionMetal version
keysArray(String)NoList of key(s) used for comparison (default: empty)v0.3+
methodStringNoMethod of comparison (default: hash)v0.3+
strategyStringNoStrategy to adopt when duplicates are found (default: first)v0.3+
conditionStringNoCondition to apply according to the selected strategy (default: empty)v0.3+

Parameters

keys

An array of strings representing the keys to be used for identifying duplicates in the rows. If no keys are provided, the entire row will be considered for duplicate checking.

method

Defines the approach for comparing rows to identify duplicates. Options include:

  • hash: Uses a hash function to generate unique values for each row based on the specified key(s).
  • exact: Compares the specified key(s) directly to find exact matches.
  • ignorecase: Performs a case-insensitive comparison of the specified key(s).

strategy

Specifies the action to take when duplicates are identified. Possible values are:

  • first: Retains the first occurrence of each duplicate row.
  • last: Retains the last occurrence of each duplicate row.
  • lowest: Keeps the duplicate row with the lowest value in a specified field defined in condition.
  • highest: Keeps the duplicate row with the highest value in a specified field defined in condition.
  • custom: Applies a user-defined logic to decide which row to keep.

condition

Determines the condition to apply based on the chosen strategy.

It can be:

  • For lowest and highest, the name of the field to evaluate.
  • For custom, a SQL predicate expression that defines the condition to retain the row (e.g., age is not null and salary > 30000).

These parameters provide flexible options for removing duplicates based on specific requirements and ensuring the integrity of the dataset.

Example

If we want to check duplicates with hash method for the rows that have the same id, contact_name adn then we keep the first row:

yaml
plans:
  my-plan:
    my-entity:
      - remove-duplicates:
          keys: # <- fields in the row to be used for comparison
            - id
            - contact_name
          method: hash # <-  method of comparison
          strategy: first # <-  'first' for keeping the first found row

schedules v0.1+ ​

This section defines the scheduled execution of plans according to a Cron expression.

The parameters that can be configured inside schedule are :

NameTypeRequiredDescriptionMetal version
planStringYname of the planv0.1+
entityStringYname of the entity in the planv0.1+
cronStringYA cron expression string, or @start for once at Metal server startupv0.1+

Example

yaml
schedules:
  run my-plan every 5 minutes:
    plan: my-plan
    entity: contact
    cron: "*/5 * * * * *"

ℹ️ TIP

By using @start as a cron expression, you can start the job once at Metal server startup.

Example:

yaml
schedules:
  run at startup:
    plan: my-plan
    entity: contact
    cron: "@start"
